base.description: The generic class on which the wildcard is based.

invert.description:
If true, then the wildcarding goes up the hierarchy to classes this one extends/implements.
(The inhertance is inverted.)

This is for the `<? super Array>` syntax in Java generics.

title:
A "wildcard class" represents the reference to a class and all classes that extend/implement it, used in generics.

For example in Java, `<? extends Array>` is a wildcard class for every class that implements the `Array` interface.
name: Code.WildcardClass
